newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey seeks end to Greek and Cypriot war games.
newsitem.headline: Turkey seeks end to Greek and Cypriot war games.

text.p: Turkey on Wednesday called on Greece and Cyprus not to repeat what it described as aggressive and provocative joint military exercises off the Turkish coast.

"We expect such exercises to end immediately. Otherwise precautions matching this kind of provocations and actions may be put on the agenda," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news briefing.
A Turkish F-16 fighter, intercepted by Greek planes, crashed on Tuesday near the eastern Aegean island of Chios during Greek war games.
One pilot was rescued and a search operation was launched for the second, Nail Erdogan.
The crash occurred on the last day of joint Greek and Cypriot military exercises -- "Nikiforos" on Cyprus and "Toxotis" in the southern Aegean.
The exercises stem from a 1993 military pact between Greece and the Cypriot government, which controls the southern, Greek-populated part of Cyprus.
"We see them (the exercises) as a military and political escalation, threatening peace and stability in the region," Atacanli said.

A dispute over the sovereignty of Aegean islands has this year put further pressure on already strained relations between Turkey and Greece, with both countries frequently issuing mutual protests about airspace violations by military aircraft.

The two countries are also at odds over the status of the divided Mediterranean island of Cyprus. Turkish troops invaded the northern third of the island in 1974 following a short-lived coup in Nicosia engineered by the military junta then ruling Greece.
